notes.title: The new Update 0.2.0 is out now
notes.content:
General
The game now uses the new Unreal Engine 5.
This will have the most impact on the lighting, you can see the effect of the new Engine features, especially during night or in caves.
The ground-alignment of the feet has been reworked along with various shader adjustments.


Environment
There are two additional natural dangers, fires and asteroid impacts.
Additionally, fires can be caused by a lightning strike during a thunderstorm or an asteroid impact.
Once a fire has started, the individual flames will spawn according to the wind direction.

Asteroid impacts are way more deadly. Every in-game day, there will be a 10% chance of such an event. If an impact happens, everything within a 500 m radius is instantly killed and a huge amount of fire will be spawned at the impact location..

Single-Player
A Single-Player mode has been implemented. This is basically the same game as the Default multiplayer server setup, but you are able to experiment around as an admin.


Quality of life
The in-game chat now stores the last 10 messages locally, you can cycle through them with the arrow up key. You are also able to cycle through the channels with the tab key.

notes.title: Devblog #4
notes.content:
Hello,
the game is now in early access, there is a new update on the horizon (no ETA).

The next update will have its primary focus on a graphics revamp with refined dinos.

Glimpse on the graphics

Here you see an example for one of the upcoming dinosaurs, which shall further expand the carnivore roster. (Ceratosaurus)
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/d7a27ba4d7cb769696ce781cd7ffeacbc5f9f670.png

Not only are there new dinosaurs, but even the old ones are currently getting updated, step by step.
Here you can see the new and refined Utahraptor model, with and without it's fluffy feathers:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/9ac14d63eb6647d4359889afc2e11147442aac16.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/d45c66d0927a711509f0ce9ce13cfb014ca7e325.png
You will also be able to decide, whether you want to have fluffy feathers or not, in the dinosaur customizer.

Game mechanics
The PVE-Content of the game will also be updated, step by step in the following updates.
To give an example: If it is night-time, and you are in a desert, your character will start to get cold and receive a "freezing" debuff. Which in turn, will increase your food consumption.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/b5c61d45f0931e8a34f176a9efebb32040ec5a0c.png
However, while being in this cold place, your dinosaur now has a chance to unlock a resistance-skill to these conditions.

notes.title: DevBlog #2
notes.content:
Fluff attack! Beware of the fluffyness.

Feathers

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/70a6ee825e629b88d819de97980af6f7d7786f7a.png

As you might know, Theropod Dinos had Feathers, and one of the Goal is to get the feathers visible on the Dinos in the Game.

There are multiple ways to achieve a feathery look.

You can draw directly Feathers on the model, but the result will look kinda flat.

Our first version of the Feathers are placed by hand and only in some key locations, like the tip of the tail or the Arms/Wings. These Feathers had a handmade Normalmap which a handmade Alpha-Map.
This was okay, but should not be the final result.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/d4ff9587970fe4c32c5e53d4431e0b57bd521abc.png
Old

Another problem was to get feathers animated on the Body, you might also know such effects from other games. It was kinda hard to find right tutorials, luckily feathers are kinda similar to fur/hair. There are much tutorials out there, how to make game ready hair, but in almost any case it was limited to the head of a human-like character. So the feathers are placed with a simple feather-mesh "hair-card" and a particle-system.  One of the missing keys to the way to body-feathers was "How to get the animations form the base-mesh to the feathers?".

Finaly the "weight-transfer" of blender was the thing which solved the problem of animating the feathers. With this tool, it was finialy possible to match the weight-painting of the model to the feathers.
To have a better, better means fluffier, look of the fluff, the new feather texture was generated using blender and it's hair-tools. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/cdbf1bf85cd57fc9c4480d0ed4496f1d21fae3a3.png


One Final Problem

There was one final problem with the Feathers. Now there was a new mesh, and also a complete different UV-mapping of the feathers, making the UV-map by hand was not an option. After few days of reserach on the internet, something called 'Data-Transfer Modifier' cached my eyes. Without become to technical, it does excatly what was needed, matching a UV-Layer of the featers to the UV-map of the base-mesh. based on the position. Only small adjustments are requied.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/408e8e688153b59390ae53d9328adc2194b37fda.png

After Some Teaks the Final result is lookm very promessing
Fluff this out:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/59cffe08e8b6e8d3e0ea316f4544dbdabc73bb6b.jpg
Ovi-Raptor:

The new Feathers where also requied forn the new Oviraptor.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/484e2f55a90d18ced39e55758c3577dff36b88c3.jpg

The Oviraptor was an small Omnivore Theropod-Dinosaur, not an egg-thief. This was a missinterpreation because it's skeleton was found on a bunch of eggs. But later the scientists found out that these eggs were it's own.

Making the Oviraptor was not an easy task and also let much space for own interpretation, because the only found skeleton was not complete. So some refernce of close relatives were used.

notes.title: DevBlog #1
notes.content:
I allways thought, to write a DevBlog is easy but i'am also worried to get too technical or to bore the readers with unintresting stuff.
What motivated me to start the project
I allways wanted to make a Game with Dinosaurs but never had the time, to dive deeper in this subject matter. I also did´nt want to start with such a project during my vocational training, to focus better on my final exames. But at the end it was itching to do so.

I started at a very young age to got interest in programming and 3-D-Modelling and did it during my School time as a Hobby, be it a tiny project for a friend or to try out something new.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/464206eeaa486e3b492c9b2b64d22a5c7d65ced3.png
An old attempt to model a Dino

Since when is the game in development?
I think it is hard to say, when the start date of an Indie-project is. Is it the first thought, to develop a game in this direction, the first prototypes or as soon as you pick an engine and type in the project name?
Well, the first plans to make a own game in this direction i had many years ago, maybe 2015. But at this point i did´nt had the time for it, because of my lifesituation and education.

Programming was at this point a Hobby and i made some experiments with the game-engine but nothing what you could call a real project.

When i was about to finish my vocational training (mid of 2018), i started to develop in a game engine first prototypes, which looked like Sanctuary Island. At this time i finished my vocational-training as a programmer and had more Time for it. 

Unluckily, i had to change the engine in the middle of 2019, because it was not a good choice for a open world game. So the game is since summer 2019 in the Unreal Engine in development but meanwhile i can't work fulltime on it.

The development
I finally could start to develop my first game, a childhooddream, with my favorite animals.
I honestly do´nt know what i could write special abou, because it feels like that 80% of the work is to research how i can implement something. But i can tell you, that it can get very emotional if you get to run for the first time a client/Server multiplayer because for a long time the only thing you see is a lot of lines of code. The Moment, you sucsessfully connect to your own dedicated server and your game model is working as it should... that shows you that the work of the past weeks was worth it.
Because i make my 3D-Modells myself, i could improve my skills.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/9bae1d168f8b0ba8fa30ef1a0118564c4cfe2f5b.png
Prototype in the old Engine

As i implement more features and the size of the playable world was growing, the old engine was not capable of it and so i had to switch to Unreal. I had to transfer my entire progress from the old one to the new. That took a lot time but it was worthwhile, because Unreal offers a large Toolset to design open world levels and is very multiplayer friendly.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/74b32fb9f2d6e07e86d22ed36cbe985e8f216982.jpg
Landscape on the Map

At the begining i was skeptical about the grafical BluePrint System of the Unreal Engine, because i was used to writing a code. But the Skepticism went away and now i dont want to miss it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/84bc0c40bc4f5aa52e9e75e823afb3f6fb962c71.png
With patience, creativiti and curiosity it seems everything is do able with Blueprints.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/e9e9ee73cd637626e1cb13965c04f7175c9c8c2a.png
Currently it looks like everything works out like planned. Lately i worked on a AI, which was running without problems on first sight. Only the pathfinding in water is not working properly, but i will find a solution.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38486816/74e79f3957d15e8d8a6cfef494f461cb5cd2c21c.png
Many, Many Bots
